attributes.body_ja:
「まま」（漢字（かんじ）では「儘（まま）」）は、「同（おな）じ状態（じょうたい）であること」を表（あらわ）す名詞（めいし）です。「まま」の前（まえ）には、連体形（れんたいけい）の言葉（ことば）が来（き）ますが、動詞（どうし）は過去形（かこけい）（タ形（けい））になることが多（おお）いです。

「まま」は、「同（おな）じ状態（じょうたい）を続（つづ）ける」や「何（なに）も変（か）えないで放（ほう）っておく」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。また、動詞（どうし）の否定形（ひていけい）ともよく一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「まま」のあとには、格助詞（かくじょし）の「に」が付（つ）くこともありますが、省略（しょうりゃく）されることが多（おお）いです。「に」は、そのあとの動詞（どうし）を特（とく）に強（つよ）く言（い）いたいときに使（つか）われます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「まま」は、「まんま」と言（い）われることもあります。これはくだけた言（い）い方（かた）なので、主（おも）に日常会話（にちじょうかいわ）の中（なか）か、くだけた文章（ぶんしょう）の中（なか）で使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
まま, coming from the kanji 儘（まま）, which means 'as it is', is a noun in Japanese that is used for describing the 'unchanged state' of something. This expression may be translated as 'while remaining (A)', 'as (A) is', or 'left in the state of (A)'. It can be used after any word in its attributive form. However, when used with verbs, it has a tendency to be used with the た (past) form most frequently.

まま often expresses that something should be left alone, or undisturbed. This is generally seen with verbs in the ない form.

Caution

While まま may be followed by the case marking particle に, it is very often omitted. When it appears, however, it will place extra emphasis on the next verb in the sentence.

Fun Fact

まま may sometimes be pronounced as まんま. However, this variation is primarily only used in casual speech, or writing that is being made to sound like casual speech.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: てある and まま(に) both describe continuing states, but differ in nuance. てある implies an action was done for a reason and that the result remains. For example, 窓が開けてある ('The window has been opened.') implies that it has been left open for a purpose. In contrast, まま(に) emphasizes that the state remains unchanged, without implying purpose, e.g. 窓を開けたまま家を出てしまった ('I left the house with the window open.').

first_relatable.title: てある
first_relatable.meaning: Something is done, Has been done, Remaining state

second_relatable.title: まま(に)
second_relatable.meaning: As is, While remaining, Left in a state

attributes.body: Both relate to a state continuing without change. まま describes a condition or state that remains as it is, neutral in tone, and when used as ないまま it means an action did not happen and that non-action continued, as in 行かないままだった ('I remained in a state of not going.'). ずじまい is especially close to ないまま but emphasizes the outcome that, after time or circumstances, the action never happened at all, often with regret or resignation, as in 結局行かずじまいだった ('In the end, I never went.').

first_relatable.title: ずじまい
first_relatable.meaning: Ended up not, Did not (in the end), Never did

second_relatable.title: まま(に)
second_relatable.meaning: As is, While remaining, Left in a state

attributes.body: まま(に) and っぱなし both describe something left in a certain state, but differ in tone. まま(に) can be neutral or passive, e.g. 電気をつけたまま寝た ('I fell asleep with the light on'). っぱなし adds a careless or irresponsible nuance, as in ドアを開けっぱなしにしないで ('Don't leave the door wide open').

first_relatable.title: まま(に)
first_relatable.meaning: As is, While remaining, Left in a state

second_relatable.title: っぱなし
second_relatable.meaning: Leaving something in a certain state, Left as is, Keep on -ing

attributes.body: きり often marks an action done once and left that way, as in 去年会ったきり連絡がない ('I haven't heard from them since we met last year'). まま(に) marks an ongoing unchanged state, as in 靴を履いたまま入らないで ('Don't enter with your shoes on'). Both can imply continuation, but きり emphasizes a cutoff point.

second_relatable.title: まま(に)
second_relatable.meaning: As is, While remaining, Left in a state

attributes.body: Both expressions refer to a persisting state, but differ in nuance. With たなり・なり, there's often (but not always) an implication that the situation is undesirable or unexpected, as in 部屋に入ったなり出てこない ('Ever since going in his room, he hasn't come out'). まま(に) also marks an unchanged state, e.g. 窓が開けたままになっている ('The window is still open'), but is more neutral in tone.

first_relatable.title: たなり・なり
first_relatable.meaning: While... ~ing, Remaining, Not or ever since, Keep or leave

second_relatable.title: まま(に)
second_relatable.meaning: As is, While remaining, Left in a state

attributes.body: Both patterns use まま, but れる・られる + ままに expresses acting in line with orders or circumstances, e.g. 言われるがままにする ('Do exactly as told'). In contrast, standalone まま(に) is used in a wider range of contexts to express an unchanged state, e.g. 窓が開けたままになっている ('The window is still open'). The compound implies passivity; the base form, a persistent state.

first_relatable.title: れる・られる + ままに
first_relatable.meaning: Do as (one is told or ordered…), In accordance with, In compliance with, Just like

second_relatable.title: まま(に)
second_relatable.meaning: As is, While remaining, Left in a state

attributes.body: まま(に) can suggest a condition continuing unchanged or doing something exactly a certain way, e.g. 指示されたままに動く ('Act exactly as instructed'). 如く・如き・如し express resemblance, e.g. 夢の如く消えた ('It vanished like a dream'). Both can involve comparison, but only 如く emphasizes similarity, and is far more formal/literary than まま(に).

first_relatable.title: まま(に)
first_relatable.meaning: As is, While remaining, Left in a state

second_relatable.title: 如く・如き・如し
second_relatable.meaning: Like, Similar to, As if, The same as
